news.title: Capturing National Security Benefits from Offshore Wind
Book Event: Lifeline by John Donnelly
How can the future of AI center human rights?
Capturing National Security Benefits from Offshore Wind
news.summary_en: Turbines, platforms, and subsea cables built for energy can also extend the reach of U.S. maritime surveillance. This report examines the evolving maritime threat environment and assesses the potential for offshore wind infrastructure to bolster national security.

news.title: Could Russia Be Poised to Use an On-Orbit Weapon Against a Commercial Satellite?
news.summary_en: Cosmos 2612 is moving into position for close-proximity operations with a U.S.-registered commercial satellite supporting Ukraine. With a history of on orbit weapons tests and gray zone aggression, Russia may be betting the West won’t respond forcefully to an attack. The West must be ready to.

news.title: Avoiding Another Long War in Yemen
news.summary_en: In the wake of the Riyadh airport attacks, Saudi Arabia risks getting sucked into another long, costly war that ultimately only emboldens the Houthis and deepens the regional conflict. Allison Minor outlines a better approach.

news.title: Rethinking the Legal Profession’s Role in Business and Human Rights
news.summary_en: With a key U.S. court path to corporate accountability closed and no federal due diligence mandate, lawyers are among the last safeguards for human rights. CSIS experts outline how counsel, bar associations, and courts can use existing professional rules to guard against rights harms and silencing tactics.

news.title: Cambodia’s Scam Center Cleanup: Is It Working?
news.summary_en: In the aftermath of 2025 Thailand-Cambodia border skirmishes, scam center operations in Cambodia has captured international attention. Cambodia has implemented new legislation, sweeping crackdowns, and international anti-scam coalition building. Are these efforts working?

news.title: “Bunker Busters”: Deep Targets, Shallow Stocks
news.summary_en: Bunker buster munitions were once a niche capability required for a small set of special targets. They have now moved into the mainstream as U.S. adversaries have responded to U.S. precision attack munitions by hardening and burying many activities.

news.title: The Future of U.S.-UK Defense Cooperation with UK Secretary of Defence Wes Streeting
news.summary_en: CSIS Europe, Russia, and Eurasia Program hosted a conversation with UK Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting on how both countries can keep deterrence credible in Europe and beyond.
